title: From “Hide and Bide” to “Loud and Proud” - The Wire China
gist: An excerpt introducing Steve Tsang and Olivia Cheung's forthcoming China's Global Strategy under Xi Jinping (Oxford University Press, September 1, 2026), which argues that China's Leninist, strongman-dominated system produces a foreign policy machine unlike those of Western democratic great powers — most strikingly in that the foreign ministry is not the pivotal institution. Only the opening paragraphs are present before the paywall.

themes.theme: Institutional structure of Chinese foreign policy

insights.claim: China's foreign policy is made and managed through an institutional structure fundamentally different from that of other great powers because it operates inside a Leninist political system dominated by a strongman leader in Xi Jinping.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Analysts modeling Beijing's next move should track party organs and Xi's personal circle rather than applying Western diplomatic-process assumptions.
insights.quote: With a Leninist political system dominated by a strongman leader, China under Xi Jinping makes and manages foreign policy using an institutional structure different from that of other great powers, particularly those in the democratic West.
